writeup: TIC 96818680 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 6.478936 days and a primary eclipse depth of 0.44 percent. The system was identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry data, with a high detection significance of 113.9 in the Box Least Squares search. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal at the target location, though with a centroid offset of 8.9 arcsec. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it has not been previously cataloged. However, an important open question remains: alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, which typically indicates the true orbital period is twice the initial measurement. While pixel-level confirmation and eclipse timing are unaffected by this analysis, this depth variation should be considered when evaluating the system's properties.
